desc:
The string s consists of the letters X and O. In one move you choose three consecutive positions of s (the window must lie fully inside the string) and turn all three of them into O. Windows may overlap and may include letters that are already O.

Return the minimum number of moves needed so that s contains no X at all.

"XXOX"     -> 2
"OOOO"     -> 0
"XOOXOOX"  -> 3
hints: Look at the leftmost X. Some move has to cover it.
Among all windows that cover the leftmost X, the one that starts exactly at that X reaches furthest to the right, so it is never worse than the others.
Scan left to right. On an X at index i, count one move and jump to i + 3; on an O move to i + 1.
editorial: Consider the first X in the string at index i. Every valid solution contains a window that covers i, and since there is no X before i, a window starting at i clears three positions that matter, while a window starting earlier wastes cells on its left. Exchange argument: replace that window by the one starting at i; everything it covered that is still relevant (positions ≥ i) stays covered.

So the algorithm is: scan; whenever an X is seen, count a move and skip the next two positions. If the window would run past the end of the string it can be slid left without covering fewer Xs, because the string has at least three characters, so the count is unaffected. Time is O(n), space O(1).
